message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo, fought on June 18, 1815, resulted in roughly **25,000–30,000 total casualties** (killed, wounded, missing) across all sides. A commonly cited estimate is:

| Side | Casualties (killed + wounded + missing) |
|------|----------------------------------------|
| French & allied (Napoleon’s forces) | ~25,000 |
| Anglo‑Dutch & Prussian (Allied forces) | ~22,000 |

These figures vary slightly depending on the source, but the consensus places the combined losses at about **47,000–50,000** when you include both sides together. The battle was one of the bloodiest single-day engagements of the Napoleonic Wars.
